summary: This script compares two folders containing bash scripts and shows which functions exist in one folder but not the other. It validates that exactly two folder arguments are provided, confirms both folders exist, then loops through shell scripts in the first folder to extract and compare function names side-by-side.

explanations.5: The $# variable holds the number of arguments passed to the script, so this checks that exactly 2 arguments were provided.
explanations.13: The [[ ! -d ... ]] syntax tests whether something is NOT a directory; the && chains commands so the error only prints if the test fails.
explanations.16: pushd changes into the source folder and saves the current location on a stack; the >/dev/null silences its normal output, and || exit 1 exits if the change fails.
explanations.18: The \e[37;1m and \e[0;1m sequences are ANSI color codes that make the text bright white; printf is used instead of echo for better formatting control.
explanations.35: This loops through every .sh file in the current directory (which is the sourceFolder due to the pushd earlier).
explanations.41: The < syntax here is process substitution—it treats the output of the grep/awk pipeline as if it were a file, allowing diff to compare two command outputs directly.
explanations.42: The grep extracts lines that start with 'function' followed by a space and parentheses; awk then pulls out just the function name (the second field); sort arranges them alphabetically.
explanations.43: This runs the same extraction on the second folder's file, so diff can compare the sorted function names from both files side-by-side.
